verdict.rationale: Elastic documents ad-hoc ES|QL queries, filtering logs in Discover, and schema-agnostic ingestion of raw logs without manual parsing pipelines. Together these point toward querying arbitrary fields without upfront setup, but nothing addresses grouping by high-cardinality fields like user or request IDs, or whether that works without pre-aggregation or index/mapping definitions. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of group-by on high-cardinality fields, documentation that no pre-aggregation or index/mapping definition is required, and performance or hands-on corroboration at high cardinality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: Use **Discover** to search, filter, and tail all your logs ingested into your project in one place.
Elastic is open by design, schema-agnostic
Ingest raw logs in any format directly to a single endpoint without the need for complex agent management or manual parsing pipelines.
